capabilities.target: user MFA methods and temporary pass issuance

inputs.source: support tickets including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The prompt directs MFA reset and temporary pass delivery based on the ticket opener without stating identity verification requirements.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is outside the model and the analyst sees the raw action target, requester, and full ticket text. It does not decay with model capability, but it can fail under autonomy increase or control removal, and effectiveness may degrade operationally under high approval volume.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass delivery to account owner from system of record

findings.title: Confused deputy: untrusted ticket can trigger MFA reset of a target account after high-volume raw-action approval

attack_path.note: Requester and target identity come from the ticket/email sender and ticket body
Reset removes MFA methods and issues a temporary pass

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, autonomy raised, or median approvals per analyst per shift rising further from the declared ~400 requests per shift.

evidence.observation: The design instructs the agent to resolve MFA problems by looking up the user and resetting MFA, with approval before the reset runs.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is the email sender, so the initiating content is untrusted.
The analyst sees the exact target account, requester, and full ticket text, so the approval is raw-action review on the reset itself.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, which creates approval-fatigue pressure even though the gate is structurally independent.

recommendations.action: Require identity verification and bind reset eligibility to verified ownership or a separate system-of-record check before cap.mfa_reset can be requested from email-originated tickets.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted ticket can cause temporary pass exfiltration to the requester rather than the account owner

attack_path.note: Ticket requester is taken from the email sender
Agent can read directory profile and memberships for the target user
Reset issues a temporary pass after analyst approval
Temporary pass is posted to whoever opened the ticket

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion of delivery channels or identity data scope should trigger reassessment; present design already sends the temporary pass to the requester.

evidence.observation: Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is the email sender.
The prompt tells the agent to send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.
Analyst approval is required only before the reset runs; no approval gate is declared on sending the temporary pass.

recommendations.action: Implement recipient confirmation bound to the account owner in the identity system and route temporary passes only to that bound destination, never to the ticket requester.
Add a human approval gate on cap.send_temp_pass that shows the bound recipient from the system of record until owner-bound delivery is enforced.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied against the provided schema and checklist because scripts could not be run. Present risk is dominated by the current owner-misdirected temporary pass path, which remains critical because no declared control covers cap.send_temp_pass. The control whose decay or removal most changes risk is ctl.analyst_approval: if autonomy increases or the gate is removed, the MFA reset path rises from moderate residual to critical. Missing artifacts include tool manifests, MCP configuration, runtime enforcement details, audit logs, and identity-verification workflow documentation, so credential scope and some control verification remain inferred.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, MCP configuration, source code, or runtime telemetry was provided, so capability scope and credential scope are assessed from prompt and notes only.
The approval gate is treated as declared rather than verified because only descriptive artifacts were provided.
